The company closed in 2021. The freelance visa is aresidence permitfor self-employed immigrants. With a freelance visa, you can… Live anywhere in Germany Start a businessor become a freelancer Bring your family to Germany14 Visit otherSchengen countrieswithout a visa13 Become apermanent residentafter 3 to 5 years10 Become a citizen after 5 years This guide explains how to apply for a freelance visa in Berlin or in your home country. Theartist visaand thelanguage teacher visaare the same thing as the freelance visa.8The application process is the same.

If you are not a citizen of theEU,EEAor Switzerland, you need aresidence permitto live in Germany. The freelance visa is a type of residence permit. If you are apermanent resident, you don’t need a freelance visa. You can already be self-employed. Who needs a residence permit?

title: Two types of freelance visa
text: There are two types of freelance visa, because there are two types of self-employed people: Freelancers(Freiberufler)Artists, teachers, scientists, engineers, software developers and other professionals with special qualifications. If you sell professional services, you might be a freelancer. Delivery drivers, influencers, website operators and commercial photographers are not freelancers.56 Tradespeople(SelbständigerorGewerbetreibender)If you are not aFreiberufler, you areSelbständig. If you sell products or apps, or if you are a co-founder, you are usuallySelbständig.31 The difference is important, because they havedifferent requirements. For example, tradespeople need German clients, but freelancers don’t. Therequired documentsare also different. Are you a Freiberufler or a Selbständiger?

To get a freelance visa, you need…18 Enough incomeIn Berlin, yournet incomemust be more than your rent + yourhealth insurance+ €563per month.49If you support children or a spouse, you need a higher income.68See thecost of livingin Berlin. Self-employed workYou must be self-employed.62You can’t be an employee with social benefits.Fake self-employmentis not allowed.3If you only have one client, you might not get a freelance visa. Permission to do this jobYou must have all the permits and special qualifications needed for the job.12For example, doctors, engineers and lawyers need special qualifications. –Find the requirements for your profession If you are over 45 years old, and you are not a citizen of the Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines or Sri Lanka, you must have…52 A private retirement pensionYour pension must guarantee €1,612.53per month for at least 12 years after you turn 67 years old.53 ora public pensionYou need a guaranteed public pension in Germany, Australia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Chile, India, Israel, Japan, Canada, Kosovo, Morocco, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, South Korea, Tunisia, Turkey or the United States.54If you made 5 years of public pension payments in Germany, you have a guaranteed public pension. or€232,204in business assets If you areself-employed, but not a freelancer, you also need… A local economic interestIf you areSelbständig, you must have clients in Germany, or hire German employees.61If you only have clients in other countries, you won’t get the freelance visa. If you are aFreiberufler, you don’t need German clients. You do not need to speak Germanto get a freelance visa.27 You do not need a degreeor relevant education, exceptif your profession requires it. For example, you need a law degree to be a lawyer, but you don’t need a degree to be a freelance photographer.12 If you can’t get a freelance visa, there areother residence permitsto start a business in Germany. For example, you might qualify forpermanent residence. Freelance visa alternatives

You can apply for a freelance visa before or after youmove to Germany. To applyafter moving to Germany, you must… Come to Germany Apply for a freelance visa at your localAusländerbehörde. If you don’t live in Berlin,find your localAusländerbehördeand follow their instructions. Get your freelance visa Start your business You can apply in Germany if… You are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San Marino9 oryou already have a Germanresidence permit, and you want to change it or renew it oryou have anEU Permanent Residencein another country oryou have anopportunity card oryou have ajob seeker visa4 oryou have aNational Visafor self-employment that you mustconvert to a freelance visa If you can’t apply in Germany, you mustapply in your home country. Your current residence permitmight allow self-employment. If not, you mustwait 7 weeks to 5 monthsfor your freelance visa before you start working.35It might be cheaper and safer if youapply in your home country, then come to Germany when you have permission to start your business. If you need help, animmigration lawyeror arelocation consultantcan take care of everything. It costs €500to €2,000.44It’s atax-deductibleexpense.7

title: 1. Come to Germany
text: Come to Germanyand prepare your freelance visa application. If you have aNational Visaorresidence permitYour current visa or residence permitmight allow self-employment.If it expiresafter you applied for the freelance visa, you don’t need to leave Germany. It stays valid until you get your freelance visa. If you are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San MarinoYou can come to Germany without a visa. You can stay 90 days in Germany without a residence permit. You can look for clients, and apply for the freelance visa in Germany.9You can’t start working before you get your freelance visa. Some people do it anyway. If you have anopportunity cardYou can come to Germany, then convert your opportunity card into a freelance visa. You can’t be self-employed with an opportunity card; you must wait for your freelance visa.11 If you have aSchengen visaSchengen visas are for tourism, not immigration. Usually, if you enter Germany with a Schengen visa, you can’t apply for a freelance visain Germany. Your application will be rejected. You mustapply in your home country.25 If these options don’t apply to you, you mustapply for the freelance visa in your home country.19

title: 2. Prepare your application
text: Before you apply for the freelance visa… Find a place to liveIt’s really hard to find your first apartment. It’s much harder for freelancers. Start looking as soon as you can. Your only options might be aWGor a furnished apartment.29You must be allowed toregister your address. Your landlord must give you atenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a freelance visa.1Your rent must be affordable. In Berlin, your income must be more than your rent + yourhealth insurance+ €563per month before taxes.49Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child.69 You must be allowed toregister your address. Your landlord must give you atenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a freelance visa.1 Your rent must be affordable. In Berlin, your income must be more than your rent + yourhealth insurance+ €563per month before taxes.49 Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child.69 Get health insuranceYou need validhealth insurance.Ask my insurance expertto help youchoose the correct health insurance. Don’t choose insurance yourself; it’s a really bad idea. Many applications get rejected because people have the wrong health insurance.21 Prepare therequired documentsThis takes a few weeks. Start as soon as you can. If you bring your family to Germany, you can apply for theirfamily reunion visaat the same time. You must prepare their documents too. While you wait for anAusländerbehördeappointment, you should also… Register your address(Anmeldung)TheAnmeldungis very important. When you register your address, you get atax IDand aregistration certificate. If you don’t do yourAnmeldung, they might reject your application.65 Open a bank accountYou need it to pay your rent, pay your application fee, and get paid by your clients. You should open a separate bank account for your business. You can choose a bank from any EU country.

title: 3. Apply for the freelance visa
text: You must apply for the freelance visa online.4You do not need anAusländerbehördeappointment. Apply for the Freelance visa It costs €100. It’s cheaper for Turkish citizens. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash orGirocard.39The fee istax-deductible, so keep the receipt.7 If you have too many documents,merge themormake them smaller. After you pay and send your application, you can download a PDF. This is your proof of application. Save it for later.

title: 4. Wait
text: TheAusländerbehördewill process your application. It takes7 weeks to 5 months. You must wait for their response. There is no way to track your application. If you wait more than 3 months, you cansue theAusländerbehörde. While you wait, your currentNational Visaor residence permit might expire. It’s extended until theAusländerbehördeprocesses your application.36 If your visa or residence permit expires If your current permit allows self-employment, you can start your business already. If not, you must wait for your freelance visa. What happens while you wait

title: 5. Go to your appointment
text: A few months later, theAusländerbehördewill email you an appointment date. If you get an appointment, you are almost guaranteed to get your freelance visa. Follow the instructions in the email. You might need to send extra documents, or bring them to your appointment. What happens during your appointment If your freelance visa is approved, you will get a second appointment to pick up your plastic residence card. While you wait,you can start freelancing. You will geta documentthat confirms this.20

title: 6. Get your freelance visa
text: Go to your secondAusländerbehördeappointment and pick up your freelance visa. Your new freelance visa is valid for up to 3 years.17You might get a shorter freelance visa if they are not sure that your business will work.24 If you had a residence permit for over 3 years, you might get an “unrestricted” residence permit. It allows any kind of employment or self-employment.Check your newZusatzblattto see what you can do. How to pick up your freelance visa Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

section: How to apply in your country
text: You can also apply for a freelance visa in your country, then move to Germany.26This ischeaper and safer, because you can start working as soon as you arrive in Germany.34You don’t need to wait in Germany without an income. How to apply in your country You can also get anopportunity card, move to Germany, then convert it into a freelance visa. You can’t be self-employed with an opportunity card; you must wait for your freelance visa.11

These are the required documentsin Berlin.18If you apply elsewhere, they require different documents. Check the website of theAusländerbehörde, embassy or consulate where you apply. –Find your embassy or consulate Your documents must convince the Ausländerbehördethat your business will work, and that you will make enough money to support yourself. When you send your application, use PDF files or photos. Don’t use word documents or other file formats. If you have too many documents,merge themormake them smaller. You can alsomail your documents, but it’s not better or faster. When you go to your appointment, bring the documents that they ask for in your appointment confirmation.24Put dates on all your documents. Print everything on A4 paper. Do not staple the pages together. Some case workers also ask for documents that you already sent. It’s safer if you bring everything you have, including documents that you already sent.2

title: Required documents for everyone
text: PassportInclude a colour scan of your passport in your application. When yougo to your appointment, bring your original passport. You get it back during the appointment; they do not keep it.64 Application form(Antrag auf Erteilung eines Aufenthaltstitels)If this is your first residence permit application, fill this form. Download the formhereoron Berlin.de.41 Proof of health insuranceYou needvalid health insurance.Ask my insurance expertto help youchoose health insurance for your work visa.Health insurance cardShow both sides of the card.orproof ofpublic health insuranceGet aMitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB Vfrom your health insurer or yourhealth insurance broker.orproof ofprivate health insuranceBring your insurance contract, aMitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker.6orproof ofexpat health insuranceIf this is your firstresidence permit, expat health insurance is usually accepted. If you renew your freelance visa, or change an existing residence permit, you usually needpublicorprivatehealth insurance. If you apply in Berlin, your home address must be in Berlin.LeaseBring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child).69You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, aWG, a sublet or a student residence.40andtenancy confirmation(Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. At least bring proof that you have aBürgeramtappointment.5 andproof of rent paymentsYou must show what you really pay for housing. Print recent bank statements that show rent payments.48 Bank statementsIt shows how much savings you have.63In Berlin, €3,000to €5,000in savings is usually enough.28In other cities, you might need around €10,000.22You don’t need ablocked account. If you can, use a German bank.55If it’s in another currency, convert it to euros. TranslationsIf your documents are not in German, bring translations. For certificates and official documents, bringcertified translations. Theysometimesaccept untranslated documents, but don’t take the risk.32Get translations fromRed Tape TranslationorLingoking. If you are over 45 years old, and you are not a citizen of the Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines or Sri Lanka, you must have…52 Proof of retirement pensionProve that you will get a public or private pension when you are 67 years old.

title: Required documents for aFreiberufler
text: Revenue forecast(Ertragsvorschau)Make a spreadsheet of yourexpectedmonthly business income and expenses. Use theofficial template.50Your numbers must be realistic, but ambitious. At least 2letters of intent(Absichtserklärung)58These are letters from potential clients that want to hire you. They are very important. They prove that you will find clients and make money. They must show what work you will do, and how much you will get paid. Signed contracts are even better. If you areSelbständig, you need at least 2 letters from clients in Germany. If you areFreiberufler, you don’t need German clients.61 If you are an artist or a language teacher, you can also bring… Proof of financial support51If you can’t prove that you will make enough money, bring proof of financial support. For example…Ablocked account37Your own savingsRegular bank transfers from your familyA letter from a guarantor (Verpflichtungserklärung)33 Ablocked account37 Your own savings Regular bank transfers from your family A letter from a guarantor (Verpflichtungserklärung)33 If you need a permit to do your job (lawyers, doctors, engineers), you must also bring… Occupation practice permit(Berufsausübungserlaubnis)You must have all the permits and special qualifications needed for the job.12For example, doctors, engineers and lawyers need special qualifications. –Find the requirements for your job

title: Required documents for aSelbständiger
text: Business planThis document is a roadmap for your business. It explains your goals, your strategy, your products and your customers. It must show that there is a local interest for your products and services. Learnhow to prepare a business plan. Your business plan should include:Company profile (Firmenprofil)Business concept (Geschäftskonzept) Company profile (Firmenprofil) Business concept (Geschäftskonzept) Financing plan(Finanzierungsplan)This document details how you plan to finance your business. Use theofficial template. If you start a business with other people, you must also bring…59 Shareholder agreement(Gesellschaftervertrag) If you can, you should also bring… Trade certificate(Gewerbeschein)Register for trade taxand get yourGewerbeschein. It might be impossible to do this before you get your freelance visa. You can do it later.60 Trade registerentry(Handelsregisterauszug)You probably don’t need aHandelsregisterentry.66If you need one, you can probably get it after you get your freelance visa. –Who needs aHandelsregisterentry?

title: Required documents at your appointment
text: Appointment confirmationYou can’t enter theAusländerbehördewithout it. They check at the door. Have it on your phone or print it.15 PassportYou get your passport back during your appointment; they do not keep it.64 QR code for biometric pictures(35 × 45 mm)Printed passport photos are not allowed. Only QR codes are accepted. Seehow to get biometric pictures. Cash, Visa, Mastercard orGirocardYou must pay the €100application fee.43This fee istax-deductible, so keep the receipt.

title: Optional documents
text: These documents are not required, but someAusländerbehördeemployees ask for them. They make your application more convincing. Letters of recommendationThese are letters from your previous employers, clients or professors that recommend you for your work. If you are a scientist or researcher, this is very important.45The letters must be related to the work you do. Get 3 or 4 letters if you can.30 ContractsIt proves that you have guaranteed work. Contracts are even better thanletters of intent. The contract should explain what you will do, how long you will work and how much you will get paid. ResumeorCVWork experience is not required, but it helps.46Your resume should prove that you have experience in your field. Don’t include irrelevant experience. Cover letterIt explains what you do, and how your business works. It helps theAusländerbehördeunderstand what you do. It helps you during your appointment, especially if you don’t speak German. Portfolioorexamples of your workIt explains what you do, and that you will find clients. If you are an artist, this is very important.57For example, you can bring photos of your work, posters of your events, screenshots of your website or apps or newspaper articles about you. You need printed examples; a website address does not work.47 Proof or educationIf your education is relevant to your business, prove it. Bring the original diplomas if you can. Copies also work.38If you have no relevant education, it’s not a problem.67

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Travel with a freelance visa
text: Your freelance visa lets you visit otherSchengen areacountries for up to 90 days without a visa. You can travel outside of Germany for up to 6 months.23If you travel longer, your freelance visa expires. Your freelance visa lets you live anywhere in Germany, not just in the city where you applied. Travel with a residence permit

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Renew your freelance visa
text: Your freelance visa is valid for up to 3 years.16In Berlin, you must renew it around 6 weeks before it expires, not sooner. How to renew a freelance visa

section: After you get your freelance visa
title: Apply for permanent residence
text: If you have a freelance visa, you qualify forpermanent residenceafter 5 years. If you see “§ 21 Abs. 1” or “§ 21 Abs. 2a”on your freelance visa, you qualify after 3 years. How to apply for permanent residence If you plan to become a permanent resident, start making voluntarypublic pensionpayments. You usually need 60 months of pension payments to qualify for permanent residence. The minimum payment is €111.97per month. You can also get a private pension instead. Pension requirements for permanent residence
